chunks: And they said: 'What! When we are dead and have become dust and bones, [then] shall we indeed be raised?'
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about resurrection after death?
ai.summary: This verse captures the literalist skepticism of the disbelievers who reduced resurrection to a physical impossibility, arguing that decayed dust and bones cannot be reassembled. In Shia exegesis, this highlights the contrast between their materialistic view of death and the divine power to recreate, a theme central to debates on bodily resurrection (ba'th al-jasad) versus spiritual immortality. The rhetorical question underscores the human tendency to limit God's creative ability to visible, physical processes.
